findings.title: Hardcoded GPG Key ID in Source Control Enables Key Enumeration
findings.impact: GPG key ID exposure enables attackers to enumerate which key was used for signing. If the key is later compromised, attackers can forge past releases or retroactively sign malicious artifacts using the known key ID.

findings.title: Groovy Build Dependency EOL Without Security Updates
findings.impact: Groovy 2.4.21 reached end-of-life in 2015 (9 years ago). No security patches are available. If a vulnerability is discovered in the codegen phase, it cannot be remediated.

findings.title: SNAPSHOT Version in Release Manifest Violates Reproducibility
findings.impact: Downstream consumers receive non-reproducible builds; artifact is development-grade, not a stable release. Each build may pull different code from the repository at build time.

findings.title: Unbounded Buffer Allocation in readBytes() Permits Denial of Service
findings.impact: An attacker can craft an AMQP message with a length-prefixed field claiming up to 2.1GB of data. The client will attempt to allocate a 2.1GB byte array, causing OutOfMemoryError and denial of service.

findings.title: Unbounded Recursion in readTable() and readArray() Permits Stack Overflow
findings.impact: An attacker can craft an AMQP message containing tables nested 10,000+ levels deep. Each level consumes stack frame space. This causes StackOverflowException and denial of service.

findings.title: SLF4J 1.7.36 End-of-Life Dependency
findings.impact: SLF4J 1.7.36 reached end-of-life in October 2022. Later versions (2.0+) include bug fixes and security hardening. Using EOL versions increases exposure to known issues.

findings.title: Silent Type Corruption in readFieldValue() Error Reporting
findings.impact: Attacker sends an AMQP message with an invalid type byte (e.g., 0xFF). The exception is thrown but does not include the actual byte value, making debugging difficult. Attackers can craft messages that trigger cryptic errors, potentially used for protocol confusion or information gathering.

findings.title: Jetty 9.4.58 End-of-Life Test Dependency
findings.impact: Jetty 9.4.x reached end-of-life. Latest version 11.0.x contains security hardening and bug fixes. Low immediate impact because Jetty is used only in test scope, not production.

defects_to_look_for.mechanism: A length field read from untrusted input decides the size of a buffer, and that buffer is created before the corresponding payload has been shown to exist.
Decoding routines call one another in a cycle with nothing counting how deep the cycle has gone, so nesting in the input controls the depth.
